raw_response:
I've been farming these 14 mu for 35 years now. I'm 56, never went to school, but I know this land better than anyone with a diploma. My husband and son both do off-farm work when they can find it — construction, odd jobs — so most days it's just me out here. We don't have a lot of cash to throw around, so I have to be careful with every yuan.

I keep 8 mu for wheat and maize, rotating them like everyone else in the village. The wheat goes in around October 10th, right after we get the maize off. I save my own wheat seed — why buy when I have good seed from last year? It doesn't cost me much, just a bit for cleaning. For fertilizer, I put down about one big bag of that compound fertilizer per mu at planting time — the kind with the three numbers on it, though I can't read them. Then when the wheat turns green in spring and looks a bit yellow, I throw on another half bag of urea. I know Old Wang down the road puts more, but fertilizer is expensive and I've learned this amount works for my land. I water three times: once before winter so the seedlings don't dry out, once when it greens up, and once when the heads are forming. Pumping costs electricity money, so I don't waste water.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest in early June. There's never enough time — sometimes we're still carrying wheat out and I'm already putting maize seed in the ground. I buy hybrid maize seed, about one small bag for every two mu, because hybrid grows better. I put down fertilizer at planting, same compound stuff but maybe a little less than wheat. If the rainy season is good I might not need to water much, but if it's dry I'll run the pump once or twice. Last year I only watered once and the yield was still acceptable.

I have 4 mu of cotton. I plant it in late April. Cotton is fussy — you have to spray for those bollworms three or four times, and once for weeds. I put some fertilizer down when I plant, about three-quarters of a bag per mu, and a little urea later when it starts flowering. I irrigate twice if it's dry. Picking cotton takes forever. Me and my husband do all of it ourselves because hired hands cost 120 yuan a day and we can't afford that for picking.

The last 2 mu is chili. We eat some fresh, dry the rest, and sell whatever's left at the county market. I don't put much fertilizer on chili — maybe half a bag per mu. It needs watering when the fruit is setting, so three times. Have to watch for insects too, spray maybe twice.

For labor, it's almost all family. During wheat harvest and when we're rushing to get maize in, we might hire two or three days of help, but we avoid it if we can. My son helps when he's not working in town.

Money is tight. Fertilizer prices went up again this year. I spend about 4,500 yuan on all the inputs. I could put more fertilizer and maybe get more yield, but what if the price drops at harvest? Then I've thrown away good money. My neighbor Li tried cutting back on fertilizer two years ago and his wheat was terrible, so I'm not going below what I know works. I'd rather put a little too much than too little — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps.
